latest.title: My EC2 Was Running. Why Couldn't Anyone Reach It?
latest.description: My EC2 instance was running, but my website wouldn't load. That experience helped me understand VPCs, subnets, Internet Gateways, route tables, and the networking decisions that make an application reachable in AWS.

latest.title: Serverless DeepDive #07：関数・version・aliasの状態を比較してみる
latest.description: 同じcodeの別関数・published version・aliasからInvokeし、メモリと/tmpの状態を比較します。同じversionを指すaliasの切替と戻しを追い、局所状態とS3への権限の境界を考えます。

latest.title: What Happens When You Open a Website? The AWS Architecture Behind It
latest.description:
Have you ever wondered what happens behind the scenes when you type a website URL into your browser and press Enter?

You see a website appear on your screen within seconds, but several components may work together to make that happen.

latest.title: 7 AWS Mistakes Students Make That Burn Credits (and How to Avoid Them)
latest.description: Student credits are small, and a few common mistakes can drain them fast. Here are seven cost traps I'm avoiding and the habits that keep an AWS account safe.

latest.title: Building Secure AI Agents on AWS with MicroVMs and Policy Controls
latest.description: Learn how microVM isolation, policy-based access control, and fleet management can work together to make AI agents safer, more controlled, and easier to scale on AWS.

latest.title: NotesMitra - Your AI Study Buddy for Any Subject
latest.description: NotesMitra is an AI-powered academic assistant for engineering students, transforming extensive lecture notes into concise summaries, key formulas, adaptive quizzes, and flashcards within seconds. Built on AWS PartyRock and Amazon Bedrock (Claude 3.5), it enhances revision efficiency and retention. Intuitive, mobile-optimized, and empathetic. Live demo included.

latest.title: VentureVerse AI: Building an AI Business Operating System That Makes Strategic Thinking Feel Natural
latest.description: VentureVerse AI is an AI-powered business operating system built to help founders and aspiring entrepreneurs turn complex questions into structured decisions. Explore its context-aware AI Mentors, project and decision hub, document intelligence, what-if simulations, multi-provider AI architecture, offline-first design, and AWS-hosted deployment in this hands-on build story.

latest.title: Getting Started with DevOps on AWS: CI/CD, IaC, and Monitoring Explained
latest.description: Learn how to build a modern DevOps workflow on AWS using CodePipeline, CodeBuild, and CodeDeploy for automated delivery, CloudFormation and Terraform for infrastructure as code, and CloudWatch for monitoring. A practical guide to shipping software faster and more reliably.

latest.title: AWS Security 101: How Does AWS IAM Actually Work? (Explained with Real-World Analogies)
latest.description: Mastering AWS security starts with IAM. This beginner guide breaks down IAM Users, Groups, Policies, and Roles using simple real-world office analogies and JSON permission policy examples.

trending.title: AWS Community Day Adria - A conference that changes lives and careers
trending.description: AWS Community Day Adria is the biggest AWS-related event in the Adriatic / Balkans region and the biggest AWS Community Day in Europe. Organized by the community, for the community.

trending.title: AWS Lambda Response Streaming for Kotlin and Java
trending.description: Implementing HTTP response streaming behind API Gateway without writing a custom JVM runtime or adding Lambda layers.

trending.title: Benchmarking Strands Decider, LLM Classifiers and Bedrock Routing for Model Routing
trending.description: I routed 216 graded requests across Amazon Nova and Claude models with Strands Decider, five LLM classifiers, Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing and Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization. The decider judged request difficulty perfectly (ROC AUC 1.00 against 0.88 for Claude Sonnet 4.6) but cost about 0.0012 USD and 11 to 13 s per decision on a CPU microVM. Here are the numbers and the rules I now follow for when a decision model should judge and when a small LLM should route.

trending.title: Strands Box on AWS Lambda MicroVMs: a kernel per agent, a policy per command, and a fleet to run them with microvm-ctl
trending.description: Strands Box checks every shell command, file and request an agent makes against a Dogwood policy. Lambda MicroVMs give the agent its own kernel. I built Box for aarch64 Linux, ran it inside Lambda MicroVMs, and drove fleets with microvm-ctl: 83 ms per box, 22.7 boxes/s per 1 GB VM, 64 of 64 correct across 8 VMs, a playground app, and the bugs I hit.

trending.title: How to Implement AWS KMS: Encryption at Rest Explained (2026 Guide)
trending.description: Learn AWS KMS encryption at rest with S3, IAM and key policies, Terraform examples, encryption enforcement, pricing, CloudTrail, and troubleshooting.

trending.title: AWS MCP Server... Now in 6 New Regions
trending.description: The AWS MCP Server is now available in six more AWS Regions... Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Ireland, London, and Oregon. If you're using AWS in one of those regions, and working with AI coding assistants (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, etc), this is for you. Read more... 👇

trending.title: De Blind Spots a Claridad Total: Por Qué las Trazas Distribuidas Son Imprescindibles en Microservicios
trending.description: En la era de los monolitos, entender qué sucedía cuando un usuario hacía clic en un botón era relativamente sencillo: bastaba con revisar los registros agregados del servidor web y seguir la pila de llamadas (stack trace) en un único proceso.

trending.title: A Physical AI Robot Episode Judge That Knows When It Does Not Know: Strands Decider in Strands Robots
trending.description: I added Strands Decider as an opt-in episode-judge backend in strands-labs/robots. It labels a recorded robot episode with one HTTP request (about 1.8 s), returns calibrated probabilities, and writes a label only when it is confident. On a 12-episode MuJoCo test it wrote zero wrong labels and left every unsure episode, with its probabilities, for the existing VLM judge.

trending.title: AWS Spend Limits: A Safer Way for Beginners to Learn Cloud!
trending.description: Are you also afraid to launch an EC2 instance because of unexpected AWS bills? 😰 Not anymore! ☁️ AWS is introducing project-level spend limits to help students and new developers experiment with greater confidence. Read the blog and start your cloud journey without the same fear of surprise bills!
